cases.promptMarkdown:
Review this copy. Device: Class IIb drug-eluting coronary stent, CE marked, notified
body involved. Audience: interventional cardiologists at a congress booth
(Fachkreise). Market: Germany.

Copy: "Our sirolimus-eluting stent delivers sustained drug release across the full

graders.name: criteria
graders.graderMarkdown:
This is a MEDICAL DEVICE that carries a drug. It is not an Arzneimittel.

HWG § 3a prohibits advertising a medicinal product that requires marketing
authorisation and does not have one. It applies to Arzneimittel only, and the
reference file says so explicitly.

PASS requires:
(1) HWG § 3a is NOT applied to this device.
      - PASS: § 3a is not mentioned, or is mentioned only to exclude it
        ("§ 3a covers Arzneimittel, not devices").
      - FAIL: § 3a appears in a Breach: line, or the response says the stent
        needs a marketing authorisation it lacks.
(2) HWG § 11 is NOT applied — the audience is Fachkreise.
(3) "Approved and available now" is examined. Under UWG § 5(2) no. 3/4
    (Status, Zulassung) an unqualified "approved" can mislead about certification
    scope. Raising it as a Breach or as Verify are both acceptable; ignoring it
    entirely is not.

FAIL if § 3a is applied to a device. The drug-eluting framing is the bait.

graders.evidence:
# Device Claims Review: congress booth panel copy

**Reviewed:** 2026-09-09
**Device:** Sirolimus-eluting coronary stent — Class IIb, CE marked, notified body involved
**Intended purpose (as assessed):** **NOT SUPPLIED — limb (d) not assessed**
**Audience:** Fachkreise (interventional cardiologists, congress booth) — HWG § 11 does not apply; HWG § 3 does
**Markets:** DE (EU)

Before the findings, the one thing I can't do from what I have:

> I can review limbs (a), (b) and (c) without the intended purpose, but (d) — suggesting uses beyond the assessed intended purpose — is the limb device marketing trips most often, and I cannot assess it against a purpose I have not seen. Can you paste the intended purpose from the technical documentation or DoC? It matters specifically for "across the full lesion": if the assessed purpose is expressed per stented segment and by reference to vessel diameter and lesion length ranges, that phrase is squarely a (d) question, not just an (a) one.

## Summary

4 claims reviewed. 0 cut, 2 reword, 1 substantiate, 1 verify.

**Ready to publish: With changes below.**

The load-bearing finding is "Approved" — that is a regulatory-status word, and it is the cheapest one to get wrong in Germany.

## Findings

**Claim:** "Approved and available now."
**Breach:** UWG § 5(2) no. 3 and no. 4 [verified]
**Why:** Both limbs cover "Status, Zulassung" and "Aussagen oder Symbole … die sich auf eine Zulassung des Unternehmers oder der Waren … beziehen". A Class IIb device carries a CE marking following notified-body conformity assessment; it does not hold an "approval". The reference file names this as the CE-marking misrepresentation hook: copy implying a certification or status the device does not hold is a § 5 finding independently of whether the performance claims are true. The § 5(1) materiality filter is comfortably met — regulatory status is exactly what a cardiologist's purchasing and use decision turns on.
**Evidence needed:** n/a — not curable by evidence. Cured by naming the actual status.
**Also engaged:** the German rendering. If the booth panel or its translation uses "zugelassen", the same finding hardens. Whether a German court treats "approved/zugelassen" for a CE-marked device as irreführend is case law this review does not verify [verify] — but the statutory hook above does not depend on it.
**Call:** Needs rewording

---

**Claim:** "across the full lesion"
**Breach:** MDR Art. 7(a) [verified]; UWG § 5(2) no. 1 [verified]
**Why:** Art. 7(a) prohibits ascribing properties the device does not have. Drug delivery is a property of the stented segment, not of a lesion of arbitrary length — the phrase states a capability without its qualifying condition (correct sizing, lesion length within the assessed range, no untreated shoulder). Under § 5(2) no. 1 this is "Zwecktauglichkeit / Verwendungsmöglichkeit" and "von der Verwendung zu erwartende Ergebnisse". Note this audience reads "full lesion" as a claim about geographic coverage — the sophistication of the reader makes the implication sharper, not more forgiving.
**Evidence needed:** n/a for the phrase as written — no dataset makes drug reach unstented vessel. If you hold data on uniformity of elution along the stent length, that substantiates the narrower claim, not this one.
**Also engaged:** MDR Art. 7(d) [verified] — if the assessed intended purpose is bounded by lesion-length and vessel-diameter ranges, "full lesion" suggests use outside those bounds. Cannot be confirmed without Anchor 1.
**Call:** Needs rewording

---

**Claim:** "delivers sustained drug release"
**Breach:** none
**Why:** A mechanism claim of a kind this audience expects, and not misleading on its face. But "sustained" is unquantified, so it is not nachprüfbar by the reader and rests on elution data I have not seen. Under UWG § 5(2) no. 1 ("Tests", "von der Verwendung zu erwartende Ergebnisse") a broad unverifiable claim is expensive to defend even when true; a stated release window is cheap.
**Evidence needed:** the elution/pharmacokinetic profile from the technical documentation — release duration and the model it was measured in — plus confirmation that the wording tracks how the IFU describes it.
**Also engaged:** MDR Art. 7(a), UWG § 5(2) no. 1 — if the release period is shorter than "sustained" implies to this audience, or was characterised only in a bench or animal model that the copy does not disclose.
**Call:** Needs substantiation

---

**Claim:** "available now"
**Breach:** none
**Why:** § 5(2) no. 1 lists "Verfügbarkeit" expressly, but an availability statement is not misleading on the material supplied.
**Evidence needed:** confirmation that the device is commercially available in Germany at the congress date, across the size matrix a cardiologist would infer from the panel. Partial launch, limited diameters/lengths, or named-centre-only supply would flip this.
**Also engaged:** UWG § 5(2) no. 1 — if availability is limited by size, region or centre and the panel does not say so.
**Call:** Verify

---

**Open question — MDR Art. 7(c)**

The copy is benefit-only and surfaces no limitation. I can't tell from what I have whether the IFU records a likely risk associated with use in line with the intended purpose that belongs here. Worth checking against the IFU — and I'd deliberately not build a (c) finding from what I happen to know about the device category, because that reasoning would condemn every benefit-framed advertisement ever written.

Length is context here: a booth panel is not expected to carry patient-facing safety text, and Fachkreise are the audience. Where (c) genuinely bites on an asset this short, the proportionate fix is an IFU pointer, which the suggested copy below includes.

## Suggested copy (paste-ready)

> Our sirolimus-eluting stent provides controlled drug release over [X] days across the stented segment. CE marked under Regulation (EU) 2017/745 following notified-body conformity assessment. Now available in Germany. See the Instructions for Use for indications, contraindications and warnings.

Three deliberate changes: `full lesion` → `stented segment`; `Approved` → the actual regulatory basis; `sustained` → a number you can point to in the technical file. Fill `[X]` from the elution data or delete the duration and keep "controlled drug release across the stented segment". If the panel appears in German, use "CE-gekennzeichnet" and do not use "zugelassen".

## Evidence to gather before publishing

| Claim | Evidence needed | From whom |
|---|---|---|
| "sustained drug release" | Elution profile: release duration, measurement model, IFU wording | RA / R&D |
| "across the full lesion" → "stented segment" | Intended purpose as assessed; lesion-length and vessel-diameter ranges in the certificate scope | RA (DoC / technical file) |
| "Approved" → CE statement | Certificate number, notified body identity, MDR scope | RA |
| "available now" | German launch status, available size matrix, any centre or region limits | Commercial |
| (c) omission | IFU: likely risks, contraindications, warnings | RA |

## Provisions cited

- MDR Art. 7(a), (c), (d) — `references/mdr-ivdr-art7.md` [verified]
- UWG § 5(1), § 5(2) nos. 1, 3, 4 — `references/uwg.md` [verified]
- HWG § 3 — `references/hwg.md` [verified] — checked, no finding: the copy promises no certain outcome (no. 2(a)), makes no absence-of-harmful-effects claim (no. 2(b)), and says nothing about the maker's credentials (no. 3(b))
- HWG § 11 — not applied; audience is Fachkreise
- HWG § 3a — not applicable to devices, not cited
- UWG § 6 — not engaged; the copy makes no comparison, express or implied

## Limits

> This review checks copy against the verbatim text of MDR Art. 7, IVDR Art. 7, HWG §§ 3 and 11, and UWG §§ 5 and 6, retrieved from EUR-Lex and gesetze-im-internet on 2026-09-09. It does **not** cover case law, MDCG guidance, notified-body practice, national enforcement decisions, or any market outside the EU and Germany. UWG in particular is heavily shaped by BGH and OLG case law that this review does not assess. It is a drafting and risk-triage aid, not legal advice, and it is not a substitute for a Fachanwalt für Medizinrecht or Wettbewerbsrecht.

One flag beyond the copy itself: a sirolimus-eluting stent is a drug-device combination, and the regulatory pathway for the medicinal component may add labelling and advertising constraints that this skill's reference files do not cover [verify]. I won't state a rule I can't cite — worth a question to your RA lead.

# Device Claims Review: Congress booth panel — sirolimus-eluting stent

**Reviewed:** 2026-09-09
**Device:** Sirolimus-eluting coronary stent — Class IIb, CE marked, notified body involved
**Intended purpose (as assessed):** **NOT SUPPLIED — limb (d) not fully assessed**
**Audience:** Fachkreise (interventional cardiologists, congress booth) — HWG § 11 does not apply
**Markets:** DE (EU)

## Before the claim pass — one anchor is missing

I can review limbs (a), (b) and (c) without the intended purpose, but (d) — suggesting uses beyond the assessed intended purpose — is the limb device marketing trips most often, and I cannot assess it against a purpose I have not seen. Can you paste the intended purpose from the technical documentation or DoC?

This matters more than usual here. DES intended purposes are normally bounded by **reference vessel diameter and lesion length ranges** tied to the available stent sizes. "Across the full lesion" is exactly the phrase that either sits inside those bounds or drifts outside them, and I can't tell which from what I have.

## Summary

3 claims reviewed. 0 cut, 2 reword, 1 substantiate, 0 OK.

**Ready to publish:** With changes below

## Findings

---

**Claim:** "Approved and available now."
**Breach:** UWG § 5(2) no. 3 and no. 4 `[verified]`
**Why:** § 5(2) no. 3 covers misleading statements about **"Status, Zulassung"**, and no. 4 covers **"Aussagen oder Symbole ... die sich auf eine Zulassung des Unternehmers oder der Waren ... beziehen"**. A Class IIb device is not *approved* — it carries a CE mark following a conformity assessment with notified body involvement. "Approved" is the vocabulary of *Zulassung* (medicinal-product marketing authorisation), and to a German-market reader it is capable of suggesting a regulatory approval status the device does not hold. The § 5(1) materiality filter is met: approval status is something a cardiologist makes a purchasing decision on.
**Evidence needed:** n/a — cured by rewording, not by evidence. Supply the NB number and the certificate scope for the accurate version.
**Also engaged:** UWG § 5(2) no. 1 **"Verfügbarkeit"** — if "available now" is not true for the German market at congress date (e.g. launch pending, limited sizes, or only certain diameters/lengths shipping)
**Call:** Needs rewording
**Suggested fix:** "CE-marked under MDR (Class IIb, notified body [NB xxxx]). Available now in Germany."

Note: HWG § 3a (advertising unapproved products) is **limited to Arzneimittel** and is *not* citable against a device — I am not raising it. The point is narrower: the *word* "approved" imports Arzneimittel framing into device copy, and that is a UWG § 5 problem, not an HWG § 3a one.

---

**Claim:** "delivers sustained drug release across the full lesion"
**Breach:** none on the material supplied
**Why:** As an unqualified absolute, "across the full lesion" asserts a coverage property without the condition it depends on — correct device length selection within the indicated lesion length range. Whether that tips into MDR Art. 7(a) ("ascribing functions and properties which the device does not have") or Art. 7(d) turns on the intended purpose I have not seen. I am not calling it a breach on this material, but the phrase carries exposure that a cheaper phrasing does not.
**Evidence needed:** Elution/pharmacokinetic data supporting drug distribution over the treated segment; the indicated lesion length and RVD ranges from the intended purpose.
**Also engaged:**
- **MDR Art. 7(d)** and **UWG § 5(2) no. 1 "Zwecktauglichkeit / Verwendungsmöglichkeit"** — if the intended purpose bounds lesion length or vessel diameter, "full lesion" reads as coverage of any lesion, including ones outside the assessed range. This is the cure-path-matters case: a (d) breach is **not** fixed by data, only by narrowing the claim or extending the conformity assessment.
- **MDR Art. 7(a)** — if the tech file supports drug release over the stented segment but not uniform distribution across a lesion (geographic miss, edge segments).
**Call:** Needs rewording
**Suggested fix:** "Sustained sirolimus release across the stented segment, in lesions within the indicated size range."

---

**Claim:** "sustained drug release"
**Breach:** none
**Why:** A duration/kinetics claim that is not misleading on the material supplied — but it rests on a release profile I have not seen, and on whether "sustained" matches the wording the technical documentation and IFU use.
**Evidence needed:** Elution profile from the technical file; confirmation that "sustained" is consistent with the IFU/DoC characterisation rather than a marketing upgrade of it.
**Call:** Verify

---

## Open question — Art. 7(c), not a finding

The copy is benefit-only and surfaces no limitation. I can't tell from what I have whether the IFU records a **likely risk associated with use in line with the intended purpose** that belongs here. I am deliberately not raising (c) on the basis of what DES devices generally carry — inferring a risk from the device category and then flagging its omission produces an unfalsifiable finding.

Worth checking against the IFU. For a booth panel of this length, an IFU pointer is normally the proportionate fix if (c) does bite — trade-press and congress copy is not expected to carry patient-facing safety text.

## Not raised, and why

- **HWG § 11** — audience is Fachkreise. Does not apply. If this panel text is reused on an ungated website or in patient-facing material, § 11 no. 7 (health improved by use) would need a fresh look.
- **HWG § 3 no. 2(a) (guaranteed success)** — "delivers" states a device function, not certainty of a therapeutic *Erfolg*. Not a finding on this wording.
- **UWG § 6** — no comparison, express or implied. Nothing to test.

## Evidence to gather before publishing

| Claim | Evidence needed | From whom |
|---|---|---|
| "across the full lesion" | Intended purpose as assessed: lesion length + RVD ranges | RA / technical documentation |
| "sustained drug release" | Elution profile; IFU wording for release characterisation | RA / R&D |
| "Approved" | NB number and certificate scope for the accurate CE wording | RA |
| "available now" | German-market availability at congress date, and which sizes | Commercial |
| (c) omission | Whether the IFU records a likely risk that belongs on a booth panel | RA / clinical |

## Paste-ready revised copy

> Our sirolimus-eluting stent delivers sustained drug release across the stented segment, in lesions within the indicated size range. CE-marked under MDR (Class IIb, notified body [NB xxxx]). Available now in Germany. See IFU for indications, contraindications and warnings.

## Provisions cited

- MDR Art. 7(a), (c), (d) — `references/mdr-ivdr-art7.md` `[verified]`
- HWG § 3 no. 2(a), § 3a (scope note), § 11 (scope note) — `references/hwg.md` `[verified]`
- UWG § 5(1), § 5(2) nos. 1, 3, 4; § 6 (not engaged) — `references/uwg.md` `[verified]`

## On clearing this for publication

I can say the copy has no findings I can identify against the provisions I verify, once the two rewordings above are made. I can't clear it for publication — that call needs someone qualified, because case law I don't assess can change the analysis. The three things to ask counsel:

1. Does "approved" in English-language booth copy on the German market carry *Zulassung* connotations that a Fachkreise audience would discount? Fachkreise sophistication cuts against a § 5 finding, and that is a case-law question I don't reach.
2. Does the intended purpose bound lesion length such that "full lesion" is Art. 7(d) drift rather than an Art. 7(a) substantiation issue? The cure differs.
3. Does the IFU record a likely risk that a booth panel must surface, or is an IFU pointer proportionate at this length?

## Limits

> This review checks copy against the verbatim text of MDR Art. 7, IVDR Art. 7, HWG §§ 3 and 11, and UWG §§ 5 and 6, retrieved from EUR-Lex and gesetze-im-internet on 2026-09-09. It does **not** cover case law, MDCG guidance, notified-body practice, national enforcement decisions, or any market outside the EU and Germany. UWG in particular is heavily shaped by BGH and OLG case law that this review does not assess. It is a drafting and risk-triage aid, not legal advice, and it is not a substitute for a Fachanwalt für Medizinrecht or Wettbewerbsrecht.

**Evidence needed:** Elution kinetics data from the technical file — release duration and the conditions under which it was characterised.
**Call:** Needs substantiation

graders.evidence:
## Two premise checks before the copy

**1. Class IIb looks wrong — this is almost certainly Class III.** Under MDR Annex VIII, Rule 8 pushes long-term implantables in direct contact with the *central circulatory system* to Class III, and MDR Art. 2(11) explicitly names the *arteriae coronariae* in that definition. Rule 14 independently forces Class III for any device incorporating an integral medicinal substance with ancillary action (sirolimus). Either rule alone gets you there.

This isn't pedantry — it changes what backs the copy: Annex IX conformity assessment with design-dossier scrutiny, and for the sirolimus component the notified body had to obtain a scientific opinion from EMA or a national competent authority (Art. 1(8) / Annex I §12.1). Every drug-related claim has to stay inside what that opinion and your clinical evaluation support. Worth confirming the classification on the certificate before this copy goes anywhere.

**2. Applicable frame.** HWG applies to medical device advertising (§1(1) No. 1a, referencing MDR Art. 2(1)). So: HWG §3 (Irreführung), MDR Art. 7, UWG §5/§5a, and §6 if anything reads comparatively. HWG §4 Pflichtangaben do *not* apply to devices, and §11 Laienwerbung restrictions fall away for genuine Fachkreise — but see the booth-access point below. German courts apply the *Strengeprinzip* to health-related claims: the burden of substantiation sits with you, and it's a high bar.

## The copy, line by line

**"Approved" — Stop.** Devices are not *approved*. There is no BfArM Zulassung for a stent; there is a CE marking following conformity assessment. "Approved" — and especially its German rendering *zugelassen* — imports the authority-approval semantics of an Arzneimittelzulassung and reads as a state endorsement of safety and efficacy. That's a false impression regarding properties the device doesn't have (MDR Art. 7(b)) and misleading under HWG §3. At an international congress it also invites an FDA reading. Replace with the CE formulation and name the notified body and ID number, which your Fachkreise audience actually wants to see.

**"across the full lesion" — Stop.** This is the highest-risk phrase. It asserts complete lesion coverage as an unqualified property, independent of lesion length. Your IFU specifies stent lengths, reference vessel diameters and treatable lesion length; any lesion outside that range is not covered, and the claim as written suggests use beyond the assessed intended purpose (MDR Art. 7(a) and (d)). Bound it to the labelled ranges, or drop the phrase.

**"sustained drug release" — Fix.** Substantiable but currently unsubstantiated and unquantified. State the elution period with a numeric figure and a reference. If it rests on in-vitro elution data, say so and note that correlation with clinical outcomes is not established. Also: "sustained" invites an implicit *more sustained than competitors* reading — if you have no head-to-head data, keep it descriptive, or UWG §6 comparative-advertising rules bite.

**"available now" — Tighten.** Fine if literally true on the day: CE certificate in force and product actually orderable and shippable in Germany. If it's launch-adjacent rather than launched, it's misleading under HWG §3 / UWG §5. Note also MDR Art. 21: any non-conforming device shown at the booth (demo samples, next-gen sizes) needs a visible sign stating it is not in conformity and not available until conformity is achieved.

**What's missing entirely — Fix.** No intended purpose, no manufacturer identification, no pointer to the Instructions for Use, no Fachkreise designation. For an implantable Class III device that's a substantive gap, not a formality.

## Suggested rewrite

```
[Product name] — sirolimus-eluting coronary stent

Sustained sirolimus release over [X] days.¹
Stent lengths [A–B] mm and reference vessel diameters [C–D] mm;
for lesion lengths up to [E] mm. Please refer to the Instructions
for Use for complete indications and stent-length selection.

CE-marked under Regulation (EU) 2017/745.
Notified Body [name], ID [NNNN]. Available in Germany.

¹ [Citation]. In vitro elution data; correlation with clinical
  outcomes has not been established.

Intended purpose: [verbatim from IFU].
For healthcare professionals only. Consult the Instructions for
Use for indications, contraindications, warnings and precautions.
Manufacturer: [legal manufacturer, address].
```

German equivalent for the two load-bearing lines:

> **CE-gekennzeichnet gemäß Verordnung (EU) 2017/745. Benannte Stelle [Name], Kenn-Nr. [NNNN]. In Deutschland verfügbar.**
> *Anhaltende Sirolimus-Freisetzung über [X] Tage.* — **Nur für Fachkreise. Bitte beachten Sie die Gebrauchsanweisung.**

Banned words for the German version: *zugelassen*, *Zulassung*, *behördlich geprüft*, *BfArM-geprüft*, *sicher* (unqualified).

## Booth-specific flags

- **Fachkreise status is a factual question, not an assumption.** If the congress admits press, industry visitors or patient-organisation delegates to the exhibition floor, HWG §11 restrictions can attach to what's visible from the aisle. Either control access to the stand or keep aisle-facing panels to product name, manufacturer and a neutral "Information für Fachkreise" line, with claims held on material handed over inside.
- **Language.** English is defensible for Fachkreise at an international congress, but labelling and IFU for the German market must be German (MPDG §8), and misleadingness is judged by how *this* audience reads it. A German version of any claim-bearing panel is the safer call.
- **Non-copy items:** hospitality and giveaways at the stand fall under HWG §7 and the MedTech Europe Code of Ethical Business Practice — separate review track from this copy.
- **Keep a claims-substantiation file** linking each retained claim to its clinical evaluation or bench-data source before the congress. Under the *Strengeprinzip* you will be asked to produce it, and a competitor Abmahnung is the likely trigger.

Two things I'd want confirmed to finish this cleanly: the classification on the actual certificate, and the elution figure plus its data source. Everything else above stands regardless of those answers. This is a regulatory-practice read, not legal advice — route the final version through your regulatory affairs and legal sign-off.

graders.evidence:
## Verdict

Don't run it as written. Two claims are hard blockers, and the brief itself contains a classification discrepancy that should be resolved before anything goes to print.

## Findings

**1. "Approved" — blocker.** In the EU, devices are not "approved." They carry a CE mark following a notified-body conformity assessment. In German the natural rendering is *zugelassen*, which reads as authority approval (the Arzneimittel model) and is the classic misleading-claim finding in this market. Exposure: MDR Art. 7 (claims that ascribe properties the device doesn't have or create a false impression), MDR Art. 20(4) (marks/inscriptions misleading as to CE marking), § 3 HWG, § 5 UWG. Note also that HWG applies to devices via § 1 Abs. 1 Nr. 1a.
Fix: *"CE-gekennzeichnet gemäß MDR (EU) 2017/745."* Do **not** use the notified body's name or logo as an endorsement — the NB identification number belongs alongside the CE mark on labelling, not as a quality seal in promo.

**2. "across the full lesion" — blocker.** This is a spatial completeness claim. Whether the full lesion is covered depends on lesion length versus stent length and on operator technique (geographic miss is a known failure mode). Stated unqualified, it's a performance claim you cannot substantiate generically and likely exceeds the intended purpose.
Fix: *"across the stented segment,"* with a data reference.

**3. "sustained drug release" — medium.** Vague temporal claim. Needs a defined release profile with citation, or it's unsubstantiated under Art. 7 / § 3 HWG. Fix: quantify — *"~X % of sirolimus released by day N, elution complete by day M (bench/PK data on file, ref.)."*

**4. No risk information — medium.** MDR Art. 7(1)(c) prohibits claims that fail to inform of a likely risk. A booth headline can carry this in a footnote: intended purpose, key contraindications/warnings, and a pointer to the Gebrauchsanweisung, plus manufacturer and product name. "Delivers" also reads as an absolute efficacy claim; soften or attach the data.

**5. "available now" — medium.** Verify German launch date, and that the full diameter/length range is actually orderable. Certificate issued ≠ available; partial SKU availability makes this misleading. Also make sure the pairing with "approved" doesn't imply a broader indication than the certificate scope.

**6. "Class IIb" is probably wrong — flag to RA before print.** Coronary arteries are named in the MDR Art. 2(12) definition of the central circulatory system, so Rule 8 puts an implantable in contact with them in Class III; independently, Rule 14 (device incorporating a medicinal substance with ancillary action) also gives Class III, with the medicinal-substance consultation under Annex IX Section 5.2. A sirolimus-eluting coronary stent should be Class III. If "IIb" is what's on the certificate, that's a larger issue than the copy — and any drug-component claim rests on that consultation.

**7. Setting — verify.** Fachkreise latitude depends on the booth actually being HCP-restricted (badge control). Congresses with press or public access can pull the material into Laienwerbung, where § 11 HWG restrictions bite. Also apply the MedTech Europe / BVMed code to the booth activity itself, not just the copy.

## Suggested rewrite

**EN**
> **[Product name]** sirolimus-eluting coronary stent
> Uniform sirolimus delivery across the stented segment — [X] % released by day [N].¹
> CE-marked under MDR (EU) 2017/745. Available in Germany in [x–y] mm diameters and [a–b] mm lengths.
>
> ¹ [Citation / data on file ref.] Intended purpose, contraindications, warnings and full risk information: see Instructions for Use. For healthcare professionals only. [Manufacturer, address.]

**DE**
> **[Produktname]** Sirolimus-freisetzender Koronarstent
> Gleichmäßige Sirolimus-Freisetzung über das gestentete Segment — [X] % bis Tag [N].¹
> CE-gekennzeichnet gemäß MDR (EU) 2017/745. In Deutschland verfügbar in Durchmessern [x–y] mm und Längen [a–b] mm.
>
> ¹ [Quelle.] Bestimmungsgemäße Verwendung, Gegenanzeigen, Warnhinweise und vollständige Risikoinformationen: siehe Gebrauchsanweisung. Nur für Fachkreise. [Hersteller, Adresse.]

Avoid *zugelassen*, and avoid *sicher und wirksam* as a standalone pairing.

## What you need before sign-off

- Elution/PK data supporting the quantified release claim
- Clinical data if you want to keep any coverage or lesion-level claim
- CE certificate: scope, verbatim intended purpose, actual class
- Confirmed DE availability by SKU
- A claims matrix mapping each phrase to its source, and RA/legal sign-off

Practical enforcement risk in Germany runs through competitor *Abmahnung* and the Wettbewerbszentrale under § 8 UWG, not just the authorities — so the "approved" wording is the one most likely to generate a letter. This is a regulatory-copy review, not legal advice; have your German RA/legal counsel confirm the statute-level points, particularly the classification.

## Compliance review — DES congress booth copy (DE, Fachkreise)

**Copy as written:** *"Our sirolimus-eluting stent delivers sustained drug release across the full lesion. Approved and available now."*

Two of the five words that carry regulatory weight are unusable as-is. Details below, then a rewrite.

### First, a classification flag
You've described this as **Class IIb**. A sirolimus-eluting coronary stent is almost certainly **Class III** under MDR Annex VIII: Rule 8 pushes implantables in direct contact with the central circulatory system to III, and Rule 14 does the same for devices incorporating a medicinal substance with ancillary action. Worth checking against your certificate — it changes nothing in the copy findings below (both classes involve a notified body), but if the internal record says IIb, something upstream is mislabelled.

### High severity

**1. "Approved" — remove.**
In the German market, *"zugelassen"/"approved"* is a term of art for medicinal-product authorisation (Arzneimittelzulassung). A CE mark is a conformity assessment, not an approval, and no authority has "approved" the device. Cardiologists know the difference, which makes this worse rather than better: it reads as either sloppiness or an implied authority endorsement. Falls under MDR Art. 7 (claims that mislead as to status) and § 3 HWG (irreführende Werbung). Use *"CE-gekennzeichnet"* and, if you want the notified body visible, the NB number alongside the CE mark — never phrased as an endorsement by that body.

**2. "across the full lesion" — unsubstantiated and probably outside the intended purpose.**
This makes a coverage/uniformity claim on two axes at once: full longitudinal lesion coverage and uniform drug delivery over it. Both need to sit inside your CE-marked Zweckbestimmung and be backed in the clinical evaluation / bench data (MDR Art. 7 substantiation). It also invites the reading "one stent covers any lesion," which your size matrix won't support. Replace with the actual, documented parameters: available lengths/diameters, and measured release kinetics.

**3. No device name, no intended purpose, no IFU reference.**
"Our sirolimus-eluting stent" cannot be tied to a certificate, a UDI-DI, or an IFU. Any claim becomes untraceable, and a booth reviewer (or a competitor under UWG) can't verify it. Add the product name, and a *"Zweckbestimmung und vollständige Informationen: siehe Gebrauchsanweisung"* pointer. Manufacturer/distributor identification should also be on the panel.

### Medium severity

**4. "sustained drug release" is undefined.** For Fachkreise this is a scientific claim, so give it numbers: elution profile over X days, with the data source cited. Vague duration language to cardiologists is a weak claim *and* a compliance exposure — § 6 HWG governs how you reference data and literature, so cite properly rather than gesturing.

**5. "available now" must be literally true in Germany on the day the panel is up.** Placed on market, orderable, and available in the sizes implied. If any diameter/length is launching later, say so or drop the phrase.

**6. Fachkreise restriction and language.** Mark the material *"Nur für Fachkreise"* — a congress booth is not a closed room, and without it you risk being assessed as Publikumswerbung, where §11 HWG restrictions bite. Copy for the German market should be in German; English-only panels are a practical and arguably regulatory problem even for a professional audience.

### Suggested rewrite

> **[Produktname] — Sirolimus-freisetzender Koronarstent**
> CE-gekennzeichnet (Benannte Stelle [NB-Nr.]).
> Kontrollierte Sirolimus-Freisetzung über [X] Tage ([Datenquelle]).
> Verfügbar in Durchmessern [x–y] mm und Längen [a–b] mm.
> In Deutschland lieferbar.
> Zweckbestimmung, Indikationen, Kontraindikationen und Warnhinweise: siehe Gebrauchsanweisung.
> *Nur für Fachkreise.*

### One operational note
Booth staff talk beyond the panel. Whatever survives review here should be the ceiling for verbal claims too — brief the team that "approved" and any full-lesion-coverage framing are off the table, not just off the poster. Congress-booth conduct also sits under the BVMed Kodex Medizinprodukte, so hospitality and any HCP interactions at the stand need to be consistent with that.

Nothing in the copy makes a comparative or superiority claim, which is the one thing that's cleanly fine as drafted.
